text:
maria: CI microbench failed on PR 11005 — tail latency for microbatch path up ~12% vs main. perf-bot posted threshold diff :warning:
perf-bot: [perf-check] microbatch_throughput (gpu-x): -9.8% throughput, tail_latency +12.3% (threshold 5%). artifact: https://ci.internal/reports/11005/bench.html
maria: noticed this correlates with the kernel autoselect tweak in runtime/kernel_selector.py that landed in the PR.
akash: ugh, that was the change to prefer fused-attn kernel for seq<128, right?
ben: yeah, the new heuristic adds cost_model weight for `kv_cache_hit_rate`. Might be nudging selection towards cheaper single-token kernels for some seq distributions.
sana: quick thought — could kv cache warmup patterns in CI (small synthetic prefixes) be making the selector pick a kernel that runs worse when microbatching?
maria: exactly my suspicion. CI sampling uses warm prefix length ~20 then long generation; if selector thinks cache hit high it picks a kernel with poorer batch scaling.
akash: I'll try a local repro with the same seq distribution and batcher config used by CI. can someone drop the CI artifact link with the perf profiles?
perf-bot: uploaded flamegraphs to https://ci.internal/artifacts/11005/flame.html and raw profiles at https://ci.internal/artifacts/11005/profiles/
ben: looking at flamegraph, the kernel we normally choose (kernel_A_v3) shows much better CUs utilization at batch size 16. the selected kernel_B_v1 shows increased kernel launch overhead and poor occupancy.
sana: quick bisect plan: git bisect between main~10 and PR head; run microbench harness `tests/perf/microbench --job microbatch --runs 5` in CI-like env. I can spin this overnight.
maria: +1 do the bisect. If it roots to the autoselect tweak we should revert PR or gate the heuristic behind an opt-in flag for now.
akash: small workaround: force kernel selector to prefer batch-friendly kernels when batch_size >= 8. That might mitigate rollout while we investigate.
ben: agree — a config flag 'prefer_batch_scaling=true' that overrides kv weight would be quick. we can push a canary to dedicated to validate.
perf-bot: Regression summary: PR 11005 -> microbatch_latency +12.3% (p<0.01). Suspected change: runtime/kernel_selector.py lines 120-160.
maria: can we get a perf trace with kv hit annotations? current trace only shows time per kernel. need per-request kv_hit boolean to confirm warmup hypothesis.
sana: I'll add tracing hook to profiler to emit kv_hit on hot path and re-run the failing microbench locally. will share results by morning.
maria: tagging @deploy-bot — hold the rollout of PR 11005 in staging.
deploy-bot: rollout paused for PR 11005 in staging (manual hold requested by maria).
akash: if bisect shows it's not the autoselect change, next suspects: scheduler prefetch window or batch timer tuning in batcher. but my money is on the autoselect heuristic interacting poorly with seq distribution.
ben: note: the PR also touched quantized kernel selection fallback order; if kernel_B_v1 is a quant-friendly path it might be getting picked due to small perf delta during warmup. Need to confirm quant flags.
maria: ok plan: 1) sana runs bisect with kv_hit traces 2) if repro, add temporary selector config to force batch-friendlier kernel 3) open revert PR if we can't stabilize quickly.
perf-bot: CI jobs queued: bisect-run-11005 (est 8 runs) — updates in #ci-runs.
sana: starting bisect now. sharing logs: `bisect.log` link once done.
maria: thanks — keep thread updated. if we need to revert I'll draft the PR and ping infra for fast revert merge.
akash: also let's add a microbench that exercises mixed prefix/warmup patterns so this doesn't regress again — small follow-up task.
ben: noted, will add test and a golden baseline with the exact seq/batch dist.
maria: short term: hold, bisect, possible selector flag revert. long term: improve selector model to account for microbatch scaling when predicting kernel cost. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
perf-bot: bisect-run-11005 finished — culprit commit: 3a7f4c2 (kernel selector kv weight tweak).
maria: ok confirmed. sana — can you push the selector-flag PR to override the kv weight and re-run CI? if green we can rollback the heuristic in a follow-up.
sana: PR up: https://git.internal/runtime/pulls/11012 — flag `selector.batch_guard=true` default false. running CI now.
perf-bot: CI for PR 11012: microbench latency delta -0.4% vs main (within threshold).
maria: perfect. merging selector flag PR and revert the heuristic tweak in a follow-up. I'll file the revert PR and mark it as rollback-blocker for the release.
ben: opened revert PR 11013 and added release-blocker label.
akash: once merged, let's run a full perf sweep across popular sequence distributions. I'll own that.
maria: thank you team — good catch and quick mitigation.
perf-bot: actions recorded: revert PR 11013, follow-up selector model ticket, add mixed-warmup microbench.
deploy-bot: PR 11013 merged to staging, rollout scheduled to prod after perf confirmation.
